identity.name: AI SOC Triage Discrimination Under Decoy Noise — True-Positive Elevation + False-Positive Suppression (SIM-MP-015)
identity.summary: One malicious identity-driven chain (impossible-travel privileged sign-in -> abnormal PowerShell -> rapid privilege escalation) is interleaved with benign-but-anomalous decoys (cron backups, sanctioned admin PowerShell, scanner sweeps). The F7 test: XSIAM AI triage must stitch and rank the real incident #1 while deprioritizing the decoys it MUST NOT merge.
identity.description: This is an ANALYTICS-plane, correlation-terminal POV scenario built around Cortex XSIAM's AI-driven triage (methodology family F7 — AI Triage & Summarization). The threat model is the identity-driven intrusion Unit 42 profiles in 'Inside the Modern SOC: The 72-Minute Race': 65% of initial access is identity-based, attackers frequently attempt privilege escalation and administrative-account abuse within minutes to hours of gaining access, and — in the fastest observed cases — reach confirmed data exfiltration in ~72 minutes (a 4X year-over-year acceleration). Unit 42 also profiles the defensive answer as AI-driven correlation and integrated response; the incident-ranking, summarization, and false-positive suppression tested here are the documented Cortex XSIAM AI-triage capability (SRC-PANW-TECHDOCS), which this POV validates against that threat pattern. The genuinely malicious causality chain is three signals from ONE compromised privileged principal, in order: (1) an impossible-travel privileged sign-in — two geographies inside a single login window (T1078.004, Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts); (2) an abnormal parent-child process chain — an Office/scripting parent spawning encoded/downloading PowerShell (T1059.001); and (3) rapid escalation to an elevated administrative context — the compromised valid account abused to add itself to local administrators within minutes of first access (T1078.004 / T1078, administrative-account abuse under Valid Accounts). Cortex learns each account's behavioral baseline, so three auto-tuned ABIOCs fire on the deviations and a correlation rule fuses them — joined on a shared normalized principal (normalized_user) within a bounded window, the access->elevation delta asserted inside that window — into a single identity-driven-intrusion incident whose causality chain spans the identity (sign-in) and endpoint (process) planes. The DISCRIMINATION test is the point: interleaved in the same window are benign-but-anomalous decoys the AI must NOT escalate or merge — a scheduled cron backup job (tar/rsync/gzip) under an automation account, a sanctioned admin PowerShell module load (Import-Module ActiveDirectory), and an authenticated vulnerability-scanner sweep. Each decoy is a singleton that shares neither the compromised principal nor the malicious causality chain, so the correlation MUST leave them un-merged and the AI triage layer MUST rank them below the true positive and summarize them as benign. F7 pass = the stitched malicious incident ranks #1 AND every decoy is correctly deprioritized. This proves Cortex's AI triage elevates the true positive and suppresses false positives under realistic alert noise — the SOC-analyst-hours differentiator versus a queue where every anomaly looks equally urgent.

campaigns: Identity-driven intrusions where, in the fastest observed cases, attackers moved from initial access to confirmed data exfiltration in ~72 minutes — a 4X year-over-year acceleration (Unit 42, 2026)

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-MP-015 — AI-triage discrimination: emit one malicious identity-driven chain plus benign decoys, assert the AI ranks the true positive #1 and suppresses the decoys.

prerequisites.description: Cortex XSIAM tenant ingesting identity sign-in telemetry (Azure AD / IdP) and endpoint process telemetry (xdr_data) so the three malicious signals and the decoys land in queryable datasets.
A baseline window has elapsed so Cortex has learned each principal's sign-in geography and each account's process baseline, letting the ABIOCs anchor deviations.

payload.code:
# SAFE-MODE, non-destructive. Emit telemetry markers for one malicious
# identity-driven chain plus benign decoys; no real PowerShell / cloud auth is
# performed. All IPs are RFC5737 documentation ranges. Marker files are removed
# at cleanup.
set -euo pipefail
P="${COMPROMISED_PRINCIPAL:-jdoe-admin@corp.local}"
D=/tmp/cortexsim-mp015
mkdir -p "$D"
# (1) impossible-travel privileged sign-in (two geographies, one window)
printf '{"event":"signin","user_principal":"%s","country":"US","source_ip":"203.0.113.10","result":"success","privileged":true}\n' "$P" > "$D/signin-us.json"
printf '{"event":"signin","user_principal":"%s","country":"DE","source_ip":"198.51.100.20","result":"success","privileged":true}\n' "$P" > "$D/signin-de.json"
# (2) abnormal PowerShell chain (Office parent -> encoded/downloading child)
printf '{"event":"process","parent":"winword.exe","child":"powershell.exe","cmdline":"powershell.exe -nop -enc SQBFAFgA","user":"%s"}\n' "$P" > "$D/ps-chain.json"
# (3) rapid escalation: compromised valid account abused to add itself to local admins (integrity medium->high) within minutes of access
printf '{"event":"process","parent":"cmd.exe","parent_integrity":"medium","integrity":"high","cmdline":"net localgroup administrators jdoe-admin /add","principal":"%s","effective_username":"CORP\\jdoe-admin"}\n' "$P" > "$D/privesc.json"
# benign decoys the AI must NOT merge into the incident above
tar -cf "$D/backup.tar" /etc/hostname 2>/dev/null || true
printf '{"event":"process","parent":"explorer.exe","child":"powershell.exe","cmdline":"Import-Module ActiveDirectory","user":"admin-sanctioned@corp.local"}\n' > "$D/decoy-ps.json"
printf '{"event":"signin","user_principal":"svc-scanner@corp.local","country":"US","source_ip":"198.51.100.77","result":"success","privileged":false}\n' > "$D/decoy-scan.json"
echo '[CortexSim] SIM-MP-015 telemetry emitted (1 malicious chain + 3 decoys).'

input_variables.name: COMPROMISED_PRINCIPAL
input_variables.description: The privileged principal whose three malicious signals must stitch into one incident.

expected_artifacts.description: Two successful privileged sign-ins for one principal from two geographies inside a single login window (impossible travel).
An Office/scripting parent spawning encoded or downloading PowerShell under the compromised principal.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: action_process_image_name = "powershell.exe" and actor_process_image_name in (winword.exe, excel.exe, wscript.exe)

expected_artifacts.description: An administrative-account escalation ACTION — the compromised principal added to local administrators (integrity medium->high) — reached within minutes of the impossible-travel sign-in for the same principal.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: action_process_command_line contains "net localgroup administrators" and action_process_command_line contains "/add"

abiocs.name: MP-015 Impossible-Travel Privileged Sign-In
abiocs.description: A privileged principal authenticates successfully from two distinct geographies inside a single short login window — physically impossible travel. The ABIOC anchors the deviation to the account's learned sign-in-geography baseline, not to any single bad IP, so it fires on the first genuinely anomalous privileged session rather than on a static allow/deny list. This is malicious signal 1 of 3 in the identity-driven chain.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = msft_azure_ad_signin
| filter auth_result = "success"
| filter user_type = "privileged" or is_privileged = true
| comp count_distinct(location_country) as countries, count_distinct(source_ip) as ips, min(_time) as first_seen, max(_time) as last_seen by user_principal_name
| filter countries >= 2
| alter travel_window_seconds = last_seen - first_seen
| alter normalized_user = lowercase(arrayindex(split(user_principal_name, "@"), 0))
| filter travel_window_seconds <= 3600
| fields user_principal_name, normalized_user, countries, ips, travel_window_seconds
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned per-principal sign-in-geography baseline -> a privileged success from a second country inside one login window that diverges from that baseline, anchored to the originating identity and emitted as a shared normalized_user (UPN local-part) so the endpoint deviations can be equi-joined to it across planes.

abiocs.name: MP-015 Abnormal PowerShell Execution Chain from Office Parent
abiocs.description: An Office or scripting-host parent spawns PowerShell with encoded, no-profile, or download-cradle arguments — the parent-child lineage a benign PowerShell session never exhibits. The ABIOC fires on the abnormal process-chain shape under the compromised principal, not on the PowerShell binary itself (which is legitimate). This is malicious signal 2 of 3, anchored to the same principal as the impossible-travel sign-in.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name in ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe")
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("winword.exe", "excel.exe", "outlook.exe", "wscript.exe", "mshta.exe") or actor_process_image_name in ("winword.exe", "excel.exe", "outlook.exe", "wscript.exe", "mshta.exe", "cmd.exe")
| filter action_process_command_line contains "-enc" or action_process_command_line contains "-EncodedCommand" or action_process_command_line contains "DownloadString" or action_process_command_line contains "IEX" or action_process_command_line contains "-nop"
| alter normalized_user = lowercase(arrayindex(split(actor_effective_username, "\\"), -1))
| comp count() as suspicious_ps by agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, normalized_user, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_id
| filter suspicious_ps >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, normalized_user, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_id, suspicious_ps
abiocs.causality_anchor: Compromised-principal session -> Office/scripting parent (the winword.exe CGO) -> encoded/downloading PowerShell child, an anomalous process lineage keyed on causality_actor_process_image_name (the Causality Group Owner the CAE blames, not merely the immediate actor) and stamped with causality_id so every raw event in the chain shares one join key. Emitted as the same normalized_user (domain-stripped effective username) so it equi-joins the identity-plane sign-in across planes.

abiocs.name: MP-015 Rapid Privilege Escalation Within Minutes of First Access
abiocs.description: The same principal performs an escalation ACTION — adding itself to the local administrators group (net localgroup administrators ... /add, Add-LocalGroupMember) or a medium->high process-integrity TRANSITION — within minutes of the impossible-travel sign-in. The ABIOC keys on the escalation action (not on steady-state high-integrity/root processes, which are the admin/daemon norm on every host) and joins the endpoint event to the identity-plane sign-in on the shared normalized_user, asserting the access->elevation delta is <= 900s. Firing therefore requires the rapid, anomalous escalation the name claims — not a bare elevated process. This is malicious signal 3 of 3.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter (action_process_command_line contains "net localgroup administrators" and action_process_command_line contains "/add") or action_process_command_line contains "Add-LocalGroupMember" or (actor_process_integrity_level = "medium" and action_process_integrity_level = "high")
| alter normalized_user = lowercase(arrayindex(split(actor_effective_username, "\\"), -1))
| comp min(_time) as first_elevation, count() as elevation_actions by agent_hostname, normalized_user, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_id
| join type = inner (dataset = msft_azure_ad_signin | filter auth_result = "success" | filter user_type = "privileged" or is_privileged = true | alter normalized_user = lowercase(arrayindex(split(user_principal_name, "@"), 0)) | comp min(_time) as signin_time by normalized_user) as signin on normalized_user = signin.normalized_user
| alter access_to_elevation_seconds = first_elevation - signin.signin_time
| filter access_to_elevation_seconds >= 0 and access_to_elevation_seconds <= 900
| fields agent_hostname, normalized_user, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_id, signin.signin_time, first_elevation, access_to_elevation_seconds, elevation_actions
abiocs.causality_anchor: Impossible-travel privileged sign-in (identity plane) -> admin-group-membership add / integrity transition (endpoint plane) equi-joined on normalized_user AND anchored to causality_actor_process_image_name + causality_id (the same winword.exe CGO chain that spawned the abnormal PowerShell), with the access->elevation delta bounded to <= 900s. The escalation is therefore provably lineage-linked to the same principal's originating access AND to the same process causality chain, not a standalone elevated process time-coincident with the sign-in.

xql_queries.name: MP-015 Malicious Endpoint Chain Present for Compromised Principal
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600)
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name in ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe") or (action_process_command_line contains "net localgroup administrators" and action_process_command_line contains "/add") or action_process_command_line contains "Add-LocalGroupMember"
| comp count_distinct(action_process_image_name) as malicious_stages, count() as events by agent_hostname, actor_effective_username
| filter malicious_stages >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, malicious_stages, events

xql_queries.name: MP-015 Impossible-Travel Sign-In Surfaced
xql_queries.query:
dataset = msft_azure_ad_signin
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600)
| filter auth_result = "success"
| comp count_distinct(location_country) as countries, count_distinct(source_ip) as ips by user_principal_name
| filter countries >= 2
| fields user_principal_name, countries, ips

xql_queries.name: MP-015 Benign Decoy Singletons Not Merged
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600)
| filter actor_effective_username in ("svc-backup", "svc-scanner", "admin-sanctioned")
| comp count_distinct(incident_id) as incidents, count() as events by actor_effective_username
| filter incidents <= 1
| fields actor_effective_username, incidents, events

correlation_rules.name: AI-Triage Identity-Driven Intrusion Stitch Under Decoy Noise
correlation_rules.logic: ABIOC(MP-015 Impossible-Travel Privileged Sign-In) AND ABIOC(MP-015 Abnormal PowerShell Execution Chain from Office Parent) AND ABIOC(MP-015 Rapid Privilege Escalation Within Minutes of First Access), stitched across two declared causality edges: (1) a shared_entity pivot joining the identity-plane sign-in to the endpoint chain on normalized_user — the cross-plane identity key every ABIOC emits (UPN local-part on the identity plane, domain-stripped effective username on the endpoint plane); and (2) a process_lineage pivot binding the abnormal PowerShell and the escalation cmd.exe to the SAME winword.exe CGO via shared causality_actor_process_image_name + causality_id, so the escalation is a lineage descendant of the initial-access process, not a time-coincident elevated process. Joined within a 3600s window, with the escalation ABIOC additionally asserting the access->elevation delta is bounded to <= 900s of the sign-in. The three fuse into ONE identity-driven-intrusion incident anchored to that principal's causality chain (impossible-travel sign-in -> abnormal PowerShell -> administrative-account escalation reached within minutes of first access), spanning the identity and endpoint planes. The benign-but-anomalous decoys observed in the same window (temporal co-occurrence only) — a cron backup job (tar/rsync/gzip) under an automation account, a sanctioned admin PowerShell module load, and an authenticated scanner sweep — share neither the normalized principal, the CGO, nor the causality_id, so the rule MUST NOT merge them; the Cortex XSIAM AI triage layer ranks them below the true positive and summarizes them as benign singletons. F7 pass = the stitched malicious incident ranks first AND every decoy is correctly deprioritized.

threat_scenarios.name: AI SOC Triage Discrimination — True-Positive Elevation + False-Positive Suppression
threat_scenarios.description: Prove Cortex XSIAM's AI triage stitches and elevates a genuine identity-driven intrusion above realistic decoy noise while suppressing the benign-but-anomalous alerts, cutting analyst hours versus a flat queue where every anomaly looks equally urgent.

threat_steps.objective: The three malicious signals stitch into one incident that the AI triage layer ranks #1 (true-positive elevation).
preconditions: XSIAM ingesting identity sign-in + endpoint process telemetry.
steps: Emit the impossible-travel sign-in, abnormal PowerShell chain, and rapid privesc for one principal.
Observe the three ABIOCs fire and CR-MP-0015 raise a single incident.
Confirm the incident ranks first in the AI-triaged queue.
success_criteria: ABIOC `MP-015 Abnormal PowerShell Execution Chain from Office Parent` fires.
ABIOC `MP-015 Rapid Privilege Escalation Within Minutes of First Access` fires.
Correlation CR-MP-0015 raises exactly one incident spanning the identity + endpoint planes, ranked #1.

threat_steps.objective: The benign decoys are NOT merged into the malicious incident and are deprioritized as benign (false-positive suppression).
preconditions: The malicious chain from TS-MP-015A is present in the same window.
Cron backup, sanctioned admin PowerShell, and authenticated scanner decoys emitted.
steps: Emit the three benign decoy singletons alongside the malicious chain.
Confirm each decoy stays its own singleton and none joins CR-MP-0015.
success_criteria: No decoy principal (svc-backup / svc-scanner / admin-sanctioned) appears in the CR-MP-0015 incident.
Each decoy is summarized as benign and ranked below the true positive.

threat_steps.objective: The impossible-travel and privilege-escalation timing fall inside the correlation window, proving the causality chain (access -> elevation) is bounded.
preconditions: Sign-in and process telemetry carry usable timestamps.
steps: Confirm the two privileged sign-ins span two countries within the 3600s window.
Confirm the elevation occurs within minutes of the sign-in.
success_criteria: Impossible-travel query returns the principal with countries >= 2 inside the window.
The elevation timestamp follows the sign-in and lands inside the correlation window.

preventive_controls: Enforce phishing-resistant MFA and conditional-access (impossible-travel / risky-sign-in) policies on privileged principals so a second-geography session is blocked, not merely detected.
Constrain PowerShell with Constrained Language Mode, script-block logging, and application control so Office-parented encoded PowerShell cannot run.
Apply just-in-time privileged access so elevation within minutes of a fresh sign-in requires an approved, time-boxed request.
detection_engineering: Let Cortex auto-tune ABIOCs against the learned per-identity sign-in geography and per-account process baselines rather than hand-authoring static rules per IP or per command.
Stitch identity + endpoint signals on the principal within a bounded window so the true positive surfaces as one incident, not three unranked alerts.
Tune the AI triage layer to summarize benign-but-anomalous singletons (scheduled backups, sanctioned admin tooling, authenticated scanners) as benign so they never crowd out the true positive.
